title: Neovim's cursor and the viewer's click select the same thing
body:
acre-gui has two notions of selection. A click selects nodes (blue outline, `Selection`) and sends `goto`; a cursor message from neovim only sets `App::cursor`, which `App::marks` draws as an orange outline.

## Proposal

- A cursor message selects the innermost node holding the cursor (not the canvas; nothing in whitespace between nodes), unless the cursor lies inside a node already selected, in which case nothing changes. That rule also absorbs the echo of the viewer's own `goto` after a click or box select. Provisional; Jack will tune it by live testing.
- The orange cursor mark goes; blue is the only outline.
- The selection remembers whether a viewer click made it. The properties panel opens only for a selection made in the viewer; a selection made by the editor cursor does everything else the same but leaves the panel closed.
- A click on empty canvas clears the selection; the next cursor move may select again. Jack accepted this.
- Visual-mode ranges selecting several nodes come later, once this is proven.
close_reason: Landed in 29eef0c. Selection::at_cursor in crates/acre-gui/src/selection.rs selects the innermost drawing node holding the cursor's byte offset and leaves a selection that already holds it. Selection::made_in_viewer gates the properties panel, and Selection::clicked carries the click logic. App::cursor, App::marks and the orange cursor outline are gone.
